content.title: About
content.content: Broccoli is an edible flower head of Brassica oleracea var. italica, widely cultivated as a vegetable. Cooked broccoli retains a bright green color, a crisp texture, and a mildly sweet, nutty flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Broccoli belongs to the cruciferous family, which also includes cabbage, cauliflower, and Brussels sprouts.
It is believed to have been domesticated in the Mediterranean region over 2,000 years ago.
Its high glucosinolate content makes it a natural source of compounds that support the body’s detoxification processes.
Broccoli is rich in vitamin C: a single serving provides more than 100 % of the daily value.
In Japan, broccoli is often served as tempura – a light batter‑fried preparation.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C is a powerful antioxidant that supports immunity and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and supports a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Phytochemical compounds
items.content: Sulforaphane and other glucosinolates have anti‑inflammatory and potentially anti‑cancer properties.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: A serving of cooked broccoli contains about 35 kcal, making it an excellent choice for weight management.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to broccoli, manifesting as skin rashes or swelling.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Broccoli contains raffinose, which can be fermented by gut bacteria and cause gas in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Interaction with medications
items.content: High amounts of vitamin K can affect the efficacy of anticoagulants such as warfarin.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Broccoli can be boiled, steamed, sautéed, or roasted. To preserve nutrients, steaming for 3–5 minutes is recommended. Serve as a side dish, add to salads, soups, pasta, or incorporate into vegetable stews.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh broccoli in the refrigerator in a perforated bag or a container with a damp towel – up to 5 days. Cooked broccoli should be kept in an airtight container in the fridge for no more than 3 days. Before use, check for signs of spoilage: discoloration, slime, or off‑odors.

content.title: About
content.content: Butter is a dairy product made by churning cream until the fat separates from the buttermilk. It has a smooth, creamy texture, a mild buttery flavor, and a characteristic aroma. Butter is used for frying, baking, making sauces, and as a spread.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditionally butter is sold as "salted" or "unsalted"; in many markets unsalted is preferred for cooking.
Quality is judged by fat content, usually 80 % or higher.
Butter has been known since ancient Rome, where it was called "butyrum".
Some countries (e.g., the Netherlands) produce flavored butters with herbs, garlic, or spices.
Butter softens at room temperature, making it easier to spread.

items.title: Source of vitamin A
items.content: Butter provides vitamin A, essential for vision and immune function.

items.title: Contains vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D in butter helps calcium absorption and supports bone health.

items.title: Contains conjugated linoleic acid (CLA)
items.content: CLA may have antioxidant properties and support metabolism.

items.title: Quick source of energy
items.content: The fats in butter are readily metabolized, providing rapid energy.

items.title: Supports skin health
items.content: Lipids and vitamins in butter help moisturize and protect the skin barrier.

items.title: High in saturated fat
items.content: Excessive intake can raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Butter may contain trace amounts of lactose, which can affect sensitive individuals.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: People allergic to milk proteins may react to butter.

items.title: Oxidation if stored improperly
items.content: When kept warm for long periods, butter can become rancid, affecting taste and aroma.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Butter is used for sautéing, baking, making sauces, spreading on bread, enriching mashed potatoes, and in desserts. It can be melted, whipped with herbs, or incorporated into dough for tenderness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store butter in the refrigerator in its original wrapper or an airtight container. A small portion can be kept at room temperature for a few days. Follow the expiration date on the package; discard butter that smells off or shows discoloration.

content.title: About
content.content: Applesauce cookie is a soft biscuit made from whole‑grain flour, sugar, butter, and natural applesauce. It has a gentle sweet flavor with a hint of apple tartness, suitable as a snack or dessert.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Applesauce retains some vitamin C and fiber found in fresh apples.
Adding fruit puree to biscuits became popular in Europe in the 19th century as a way to increase moisture and shelf life.
Applesauce cookies are often used in children's meals because of their soft texture and moderate sweetness.
The combination of whole‑grain flour and applesauce makes the product more nutritious than standard sugary cookies.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Applesauce and whole‑grain flour provide dietary fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: A small amount of vitamin C from the applesauce helps support the immune system.

items.title: Low in trans fats
items.content: When made with non‑hydrogenated butter, the cookie contains no trans fats.

items.title: Moderate sugar level
items.content: Added sugar is balanced with the natural sweetness of applesauce, lowering the overall glycemic impact.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Phenolic compounds from apples provide antioxidant benefits.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: The cookie contains gluten and is not suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although some sugar is replaced by applesauce, the product still contains added sugar and should be limited for diabetics.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Some commercial versions may include preservatives; check the label if you avoid them.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Applesauce cookies can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, added to yogurt, used in baby food, or as a base for dessert tarts. For extra aroma, warm them briefly before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cookies in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer storage (over 2 weeks) keep them refrigerated to maintain freshness and prevent drying out.

content.title: About
content.content: Fruit mixture, frozen is a ready‑to‑use blend of diced berries and tropical fruits (strawberry, raspberry, blueberry, pineapple, mango) that are flash‑frozen at low temperature to preserve flavor, aroma and nutrients. The mix is convenient for smoothies, desserts, baking or simply as a refreshing snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The blend contains 100 % natural fruit with no added sugar, preservatives or artificial flavors.
IQF (individually quick frozen) technology retains over 90 % of vitamin C and other antioxidants.
The mixture is widely used in professional kitchens to speed up dish preparation.
It is suitable for vegetarians and vegans.
Packaging is usually made from recyclable PET material.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Berries provide anthocyanins and polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and contributes to satiety.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and heart function.

items.title: Low‑calorie snack
items.content: The mix is low in fat and calories, making it suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Allergy to specific fruits
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to strawberry, mango or pineapple.

items.title: Natural sugar content
items.content: Although no sugar is added, the natural sugars in the fruit can affect blood glucose levels in people with diabetes.

items.title: Improper storage
items.content: If the mixture thaws and refreezes, quality may degrade and microbial risk can increase.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add the mix to smoothies, yogurt, oatmeal, use it in baked goods (muffins, cakes) or simply thaw and enjoy as a refreshing dessert. For extra sweetness, drizzle with honey or maple syrup.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in the freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. After opening, use within 3–4 months. Do not thaw and refreeze to maintain texture and safety.

hot-chocolate-cocoa-dry-mix-reduced-suga.title: Hot chocolate / cocoa, dry mix, reduced sugar, made with low‑fat (1 %) or fat‑free (skim) milk

content.title: About
content.content: The dry mix for hot chocolate/cocoa contains cocoa mass, a reduced‑sugar sweetener, and low‑fat (1 %) or skim milk powder. It dissolves quickly in hot water or milk, creating a smooth, chocolate‑flavored beverage with lower calories.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The mix is formulated for those who watch their sugar intake but still want a chocolate taste.
Low‑fat milk retains protein and calcium while cutting down on fat.
Cocoa mass is rich in flavonoids, which have antioxidant properties.
The dry form allows long shelf life without quality loss.
Convenient for office, travel, or home use.

items.title: Lower blood‑sugar impact
items.content: The reduced‑sugar sweetener helps lower the glycemic response compared with regular hot chocolate.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Cocoa provides flavonoids that may support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Calcium and protein
items.content: Skim milk powder supplies calcium and high‑quality protein important for bones and muscles.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: The mix contains minimal fat, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Mood enhancement
items.content: Cocoa stimulates serotonin and endorphin production, which can improve mood.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: The product contains milk protein, so individuals with dairy allergy should avoid it.

items.title: Caffeine content
items.content: Cocoa contains a small amount of caffeine; caffeine‑sensitive persons should consider this.

items.title: Sweetener sensitivity
items.content: Some reduced‑sugar sweeteners may cause gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Prepare
content.content: Mix 2 tsp of the dry mix with 200 ml of hot water or milk, stir until fully dissolved. Optionally add a splash of low‑fat cream or extra sweetener to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the dry mix in a sealed container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Refer to the package for the best‑by date.

kidney-beans-from-canned-fat-added.title: Kidney beans, from canned, fat added

content.title: About
content.content: Canned kidney beans with added fat are a ready‑to‑eat product made from whole beans that are blanched, cooked, and then sealed in their own liquid with the addition of vegetable oil. The beans have a rich, slightly sweet flavor and a firm texture, while the added fat increases caloric density and makes them more satisfying.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Kidney beans are named for their characteristic kidney‑shaped seeds.
Canning preserves the beans for several years while retaining most nutrients.
Added oil enhances the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as vitamin E.
Beans are a staple protein source in vegetarian and vegan diets.
In the United States canned kidney beans are commonly used in chili, salads, and soups.

items.title: Rich source of plant protein
items.content: A 100 g serving provides about 7 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, helps regulate blood sugar, and promotes satiety.

items.title: Contains iron and folate
items.content: These micronutrients are essential for blood formation and preventing anemia.

items.title: Source of plant antioxidants
items.content: Kidney beans contain polyphenols that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Improved absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins
items.content: The added oil helps the body absorb vitamins A, D, E, and K more efficiently.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned foods often contain added salt; people with hypertension should choose low‑sodium versions.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Toxin in raw beans
items.content: Raw or undercooked kidney beans contain phytohaemagglutinin, a toxin that is destroyed during proper cooking and canning.

items.title: High caloric density
items.content: The added fat raises the calorie count, which may be a concern for weight management.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The beans are ready straight from the can: add them to salads, chili, soups, stews, or use as a filling for tacos. They can also be quickly warmed in a skillet with vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer beans to an airtight container and keep refrigerated for 3–4 days. Discard if an off‑odor or discoloration develops.

content.title: About
content.content: Condensed sweetened milk is a thick milk product made by evaporating whole milk and adding sugar. It has a sweet, caramel-like flavor and a creamy texture, commonly used in desserts, beverages, and confectionery.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Condensed milk was invented in the 19th century as a way to preserve milk without refrigeration.
Sweetened condensed milk is a key ingredient in traditional dishes worldwide, such as Brazilian brigadeiro or Indian kulfi.
During evaporation, lactose concentration increases, enhancing the product’s sweetness.
It can replace fresh milk in recipes that require a thick consistency.
Some markets offer unsweetened versions, usually labeled as "unsweetened".

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Condensed milk provides calcium, essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains vitamins B2 and B12, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: High sugar and fat content offers a quick source of energy.

items.title: Protein
items.content: Milk protein contributes to tissue building and repair.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Small amounts of phosphorus and magnesium support various bodily functions.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive intake may lead to weight gain and increase diabetes risk.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience discomfort after consumption.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to milk proteins can have allergic reactions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Condensed milk is very calorie‑dense, so portion control is important.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use condensed milk in baking, for making custards, toppings, in coffee, ice cream, or as a sweet filling for pancakes and waffles. It can be stirred into hot tea or blended into milkshakes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened can in a cool, dry place. Once opened, keep it refrigerated and consume within 1‑2 weeks. Discard if it develops off‑flavors, discoloration, or signs of fermentation.

content.title: About
content.content: Mirepoix is a classic blend of finely diced vegetables—typically onion, carrot and celery—sautéed until soft. Cooked mirepoix is used as an aromatic base for sauces, soups, stews and many other dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The traditional French mixture is named after the town of Mirepoix in Normandy.
Classic ratio: 2 parts onion, 1 part carrot, 1 part celery.
Cooked mirepoix is often sold frozen, preserving flavor and saving prep time.
Variations may include leeks, garlic, bell pepper or tomatoes.
Mirepoix forms the foundation of over 80 % of classic French sauces.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: The vegetables provide dietary fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Low‑calorie flavor enhancer
items.content: Mirepoix adds depth of taste without significantly increasing a dish’s calorie count.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Onion, carrot and celery supply vitamin C, vitamin K, folate and potassium.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Beta‑carotene from carrots and flavonoids from onions act as antioxidants.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: The combination of vitamins and phytochemicals helps bolster the immune system.

items.title: Celery allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to celery, a component of mirepoix.

items.title: Sodium content in prepared product
items.content: Frozen cooked mirepoix can contain added salt; people with hypertension should check the label.

items.title: Nutrient loss during long storage
items.content: Extended freezing may reduce vitamin C levels.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Add the cooked mirepoix to a hot pan with a little oil, sauté 5‑7 minutes until golden, then continue with the main recipe. It works well in béchamel, tomato sauces, soups, stews, risotto and meat dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen mirepoix in an airtight bag at –18 °C. After thawing, use within 2‑3 days and store in the refrigerator in a sealed container. Discard if any off‑odors develop.

content.title: About
content.content: Summer squash (Zucchini) is a young, tender variety of squash, usually light green or yellow. When cooked it retains a soft texture and a mild sweet flavor. It is used in soups, stews, side dishes and as an ingredient in baked goods.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Summer squash belongs to the Cucurbitaceae family and is a close relative of cucumber.
Unlike mature pumpkins, young fruits contain less sugar and more water.
In Italy it is called “zucchini” and often served as “zoodles” – thin strips used like pasta.
Summer squash is rich in antioxidants, especially lutein and zeaxanthin.
In Japan it appears in the traditional dish “kabu-no-tai” (stewed squash).

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Cooked summer squash provides about 17 kcal per 100 g, making it an excellent choice for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of vitamin A as beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene is important for eye health and skin.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure and supports muscle function.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber improves digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to summer squash.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: When buying non‑organic squash, rinse thoroughly to reduce pesticide exposure.

items.title: Excess sodium from added salt
items.content: Adding salt during cooking can increase sodium content, which should be limited in hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Summer squash can be boiled, steamed, roasted, or sautéed. It is added to soups, stews, salads, pasta dishes, and used as a filling for pancakes or pies. Before cooking, trim the ends and cut into cubes, slices, or ribbons.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked summer squash in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3–4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags – it keeps its flavor and texture for up to 2 months.

turkey-with-gravy-dressing-potatoes-vege.title: Turkey with Gravy, Dressing, Potatoes and Vegetables (Frozen Meal)

content.title: About
content.content: Turkey with gravy, dressing, potatoes and vegetables is a ready‑to‑heat frozen meal designed for quick preparation in a microwave or oven. It contains a portion of turkey breast covered in a savory gravy, a side of potatoes, mixed vegetables, and a creamy dressing. One serving provides roughly 350 kcal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turkey is one of the leanest meats and is often used in health‑focused diets.
Frozen ready meals save time while preserving flavor when stored properly at –18 °C.
The gravy is made from chicken broth and aromatic herbs, giving it a rich taste.
The combination of potatoes and vegetables offers a balance of carbs, fiber, and vitamins.
This product was launched in 2023 as part of the “Quick Dinner” line.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Turkey breast contains very little saturated fat, making the meal suitable for heart‑healthy eating.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A single serving delivers about 25 g of protein, essential for muscle repair and satiety.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Turkey provides vitamin B6 and niacin, which support metabolism.

items.title: Fiber from vegetables and potatoes
items.content: Helps regulate digestion and maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: The meat supplies heme iron, important for hemoglobin formation.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared sauces often contain added salt; people monitoring blood pressure should account for this.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to turkey.

items.title: Proper heating required
items.content: Uneven heating can leave cold spots where bacteria may survive.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: The product may contain stabilizers and antioxidants that are not suitable for everyone.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the meal in the microwave for about 3–4 minutes or in a conventional oven at 180 °C for roughly 20 minutes. Stir before serving to coat the turkey and sides evenly with gravy. For extra freshness, garnish with chopped herbs or a squeeze of lemon.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen meal at –18 °C or lower. Once thawed, consume within 2 hours and do not refreeze. Discard if you notice off‑odors or discoloration.
